summary: This article explains how Taiwan became a dominant force in the global semiconductor industry, despite starting as an agricultural economy. It attributes Taiwan's success to globalization's impact on electronics, East Asia's skilled workforce and infrastructure, and a unique business model focused on contract manufacturing rather than brand development. The piece highlights TSMC's role in supplying advanced chips globally, creating a significant dependency on Taiwan.

title: TSMC Trims Capital Spending Forecast Amid Chip Headwinds
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) announced a 10% cut in its capital expenditure forecast for the current year. This decision comes despite the company reporting an 80% increase in net income for the July-to-September quarter, driven by strong sales of advanced chips. The revised forecast reflects global chip demand slowdown and rising costs impacting the world's largest contract chip manufacturer.

title: The Chips That Make Taiwan the Center of the World
summary: This article examines Taiwan's critical role in the global semiconductor industry, particularly through TSMC, and the geopolitical risks associated with its dependence on the island amid rising U.S.-China tensions. It explores the potential catastrophic economic consequences for the world if military action or political pressure disrupts Taiwan's chip manufacturing capabilities. The author argues that while Taiwan's chip industry provides a "silicon shield," it also makes the island a crucial target in any conflict.

title: Taiwan’s Semiconductor Dilemma
summary: Taiwan's robust semiconductor industry, a major global strength, is paradoxically becoming a political vulnerability as the world seeks to reduce its dependence on the island for microchip manufacturing. While awareness of threats to Taiwan is at a 50-year high, overemphasizing its role in the global electronics supply chain could backfire, potentially diminishing international interest in its security once chip production diversifies. The article warns against narratives that might prompt a global effort to move semiconductor production out of Taiwan, which could harm its economy in the long run.

title: TSMC and Sony partner to build US$7bn chip factory in Japan
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and Sony have announced a joint venture to build a $7 billion chip plant in Japan, aiming for mass production by 2024. The new factory in Kumamoto will be TSMC's first in Japan, creating 1,500 high-tech jobs and producing 45,000 12-inch wafers per month to address the global semiconductor shortage. Sony will invest $500 million for a 20% equity stake, with significant funding also provided by the Japanese government.

title: Taiwan Chip Giant to Expand to Japan
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) announced plans to build a new plant in Japan, aiming to begin operations in 2024. This move is expected to bolster Japan's chipmaking sector and economic security, with the Japanese government subsidizing approximately half of TSMC's $8.81 billion project. The expansion is also seen as a strategic move to decrease reliance on China and diversify the global semiconductor supply chain due to increasing geopolitical tensions.
source: VOA - Voice of America English News

title: Inside TSMC, the Taiwanese chipmaking giant that's building a new plant in Phoenix
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is investing $100 billion to ramp up chip production and address the global chip shortage. The company is building a $12 billion fabrication plant in Phoenix, Arizona, set to produce 5-nanometer chips in 2024, aiming to bring advanced chip manufacturing back to the U.S. TSMC, a "pure-play foundry," dominates the advanced chip market and is a key supplier for companies like Apple, making its expansion crucial for global technology supply chains and national security.

title: TSMC says semiconductor capacity will remain tight into 2022
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) expects semiconductor capacity to remain tight throughout 2021 and into 2022 due to strong demand, despite efforts to increase production. While the automotive sector's chip shortage is projected to reduce this quarter, the company notes that it will take time for improvements to reach OEMs given the complex supply chain. TSMC is investing $100 billion over three years to expand capacity, anticipating continued reliance on its products for safer, greener, and smarter vehicles.

title: Implications of US-China Tech War for Taiwan’s Semiconductors Industry
summary: Taiwan's semiconductor industry, particularly TSMC, has gained significant global attention amidst worsening US-China relations, highlighting its critical role in advanced technology and global industrial activity. However, both US and Chinese ambitions for self-sufficiency in semiconductor production threaten Taiwan's business model and could eventually create friction for its firms. Taiwan's government must strategize to position its tech dominance as a partnership rather than a risk to ensure its continued viability.

title: Taiwan, Chips, and Geopolitics: Part 1
summary: This article examines Taiwan's critical role in the global semiconductor supply chain, particularly through TSMC, and its implications for U.S. and China's Taiwan policies. It analyzes how TSMC's dominance, while significant, may not fundamentally alter Beijing's "Taiwan problem" calculus or third-party governments' approaches. The article delves into the complexities of the semiconductor value chain and why TSMC has become indispensable for cutting-edge logic chip manufacturing.
source: The Diplomat – Asia-Pacific Current Affairs Magazine

title: Shares of Taiwan’s TSMC soar after Intel’s apparent retreat in chip manufacturing
summary: Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) rallied significantly after Intel signaled a potential shift away from manufacturing its own chip components, possibly outsourcing to TSMC. This surge made TSMC the 12th most valuable stock globally, briefly surpassing Walmart, and added over US$30 billion to its market capitalization. The event underscores TSMC's growing influence in the global semiconductor industry and its impact on Taiwan's stock market.

title: TSMC Announces Intention to Build and Operate an Advanced Semiconductor Fab in the United States
summary: TSMC announced its plan to build and operate an advanced semiconductor fab in the U.S. state of Arizona. This facility will use 5nm technology, have a capacity of 20,000 wafers per month, create over 1,600 high-tech jobs directly, and involves a total investment of approximately US$12 billion from 2021 to 2029. The project is strategically important for the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem and relies on continued U.S. federal government and Arizona state support.

title: TSMC’s Announcement Of A New U.S. Semiconductor Fab Is Big News
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) announced plans to build a new semiconductor fabrication facility (fab) in Arizona, a move deemed significant despite its initial limited scale. This investment, estimated at $12 billion for a 5 nm technology fab, highlights the challenges and costs of advanced semiconductor manufacturing. While a welcome development for the U.S. supply chain, it represents only a small step towards securing domestic semiconductor production, as the U.S. will still rely heavily on Asian facilities for capacity and specialized processes like packaging.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Taiwan Firm to Build Chip Factory in U.S.
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) announced plans to build a $12 billion chip factory in Arizona. This move comes as the U.S. seeks to reduce its dependence on Asian countries for critical microelectronics. The project has support from both the federal government and the state of Arizona.

title: Can Taiwan keep its perch as top chip manufacturer?
summary: Taiwan's journey to becoming a top chip manufacturer began in 1974 with a US$10 million investment and a crucial technology transfer from RCA in 1976. This article, part of a series, examines Taiwan's rise in chip production with US help and the current challenges it faces, particularly from China, as detailed by key figures like MediaTek chairman Tsai Ming-kai.

title: Globalfoundries Launches Legal Battle Against Taiwan Semiconductor, Also Targets Manufacturers
summary: Globalfoundries has initiated a multi-front legal attack against Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), seeking a U.S. import ban that could impact various electronic devices. The company filed 25 complaints in multiple courts and with the U.S. International Trade Commission, alleging TSMC violated over a dozen patents related to chip manufacturing. This legal action targets not only TSMC but also device manufacturers using their chips, like Apple and Lenovo.

title: China's biggest chipmaker is still years behind its global rivals
summary: SMIC, China's largest chipmaker, remains several years behind global rivals like TSMC in advanced chip technology, particularly 7nm chips, despite significant government investment and initiatives like "Made In China 2025." While China aims for greater self-sufficiency in semiconductor production due to the ongoing trade war with the U.S., analysts note that SMIC's technological gap and the need for greater talent and investment pose challenges to closing this disparity for at least another decade. Some factors, such as the slowing pace of chip miniaturization and leadership changes, could potentially help SMIC narrow the gap.

title: Chipmaker TSMC is set back by a bad photoresist
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) experienced a production halt due to a defective batch of photoresist, a critical material in chip manufacturing. This incident highlights the semiconductor industry's reliance on high-purity material suppliers and the potential ramifications of quality control issues. TSMC expects to recover the lost production in the coming months, attributing the problem to a subtle variation in the photoresist component rather than a contaminant.

title: TSMC Chip Maker Blames WannaCry Malware for Production Halt
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) experienced a production halt across several chip-fabrication factories due to a variant of the WannaCry malware. The cyberattack, which was not a direct hack but rather an infection spread through tainted software installed by a supplier, is expected to impact revenue by approximately $256 million and cause shipment delays. Although full operations have resumed, the incident raises concerns, especially for key customers like Apple, for whom TSMC is a sole supplier of SoC components.

title: Apple chip supplier TSMC resumes production after WannaCry attack
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd (TSMC) announced it has fully resumed production after a WannaCry ransomware attack temporarily shut down some of its computer systems. The incident, caused by an "operational error" during installation, is expected to cause a 2% impact on its third-quarter revenue, down from an initial 3% estimate, but is not expected to affect its annual revenue growth forecast. TSMC assured that neither its data manufacturing base nor client information were compromised.

title: Cryptocurrency mining is now so big it’s showing up in the earnings of the world’s largest chipmaker
summary: Cryptocurrency mining is significantly impacting the earnings of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest contract chipmaker. TSMC reported revenues driven by demand from crypto miners for the second consecutive quarter, with an estimated $350-$400 million in revenue from this sector in the previous reporting period, primarily from Bitmain. Despite management's cautious outlook on forecasting future crypto demand, TSMC views deep learning and blockchain technologies as key drivers for semiconductor innovation.

title: Firms face China challenge: C.C. Wei
summary: C.C. Wei, cochief executive of TSMC and director-general of the Taiwan Semiconductor Industry Association (TSIA), warned that Taiwan's semiconductor industry faces escalating global competition and challenges from China's rising chip industry. He emphasized that while artificial intelligence presents significant opportunities, Taiwanese companies must differentiate themselves technologically and politically, TSIA will work with the government to ensure a stable supply of resources and talent. Companies like Powertech Technology Inc. are urged to consolidate and innovate to combat increasing competition from Chinese rivals.

title: Semiconductor Industry To Lose Titan As Morris Chang Sets TSMC Retirement Date
summary: Morris Chang, the influential chairman of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC), has announced his retirement effective June 2018. Chang, 86, is recognized as a titan in the chip industry, having founded TSMC and built it into a leader in specialized semiconductor contract manufacturing for companies like Apple, Nvidia, and Qualcomm. He was previously named Forbes Asia's Businessman of the Year in 2012 and selected as one of the world's 100 greatest living business minds by Forbes.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Mfg. Co. Ltd. Says 5-Nano Tech to Enter Risk Production in 2019
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) announced plans to begin "risk production" of its 5-nanometer technology in the first half of 2019, with mass production expected by the first half of 2020. This advancement aligns with Moore's Law and is crucial for TSMC to satisfy customer demand for advanced, power-efficient chips, particularly for high-end smartphones and data centers. The company aims to maintain or grow market share by consistently delivering industry-leading chip density, though execution risk remains a factor in such technology transitions.

title: TSMC Ranked No. 1 in Semiconductor Manufacturing by IEEE Spectrum Patent Power Scorecard
summary: TSMC announced it earned the highest ranking in the Semiconductor Manufacturing Sector in IEEE Spectrum magazine’s “Patent Power Scorecard” for the second consecutive year. This achievement affirms TSMC's strong technology innovation, patent portfolio, and strategy. The company invests billions annually in R&D, and this recognition highlights its long-term efforts in protecting intellectual property and creating patent value.

title: Lights out for TSMC Solar
summary: TSMC announced that its subsidiary, TSMC Solar, will cease manufacturing operations at the end of August 2015, citing that the solar business is no longer viable despite world-class conversion efficiency. The company attributed the failure to its late market entry and lack of economies of scale, leading to a substantial cost disadvantage. Remaining solar panel inventory will be installed at TSMC facilities, and employees will be offered jobs within TSMC in Taiwan.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Earnings Growth Slows
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) reported its slowest earnings growth in a year for the second quarter, attributed to increased competition and a slowdown in global smartphone demand. Despite a 33% rise in net profit to NT$79.42 billion (US$2.56 billion), exceeding analyst expectations, and a 12% revenue increase to NT$205.44 billion, the company is facing challenges as it loses some orders to rivals.

title: Chip designer Arm slips after disappointing Taiwan Semiconductor results
summary: Chip designer Arm's stock fell 4p to £10.41 after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) reported disappointing revenue figures for June, which were down 14.5% compared to May and 0.6% year-over-year. Liberum reiterated a 'sell' recommendation on Arm, highlighting the close correlation between TSMC's performance and Arm's due to most Arm-technology chips being manufactured by TSMC.

title: TSMC looking at new materials, transistor structures for sub-10nm tech
summary: TSMC is actively researching new materials and transistor structures for its sub-10nm fabrication processes, expected between 2017 and 2019. This push mirrors efforts by rivals Intel and Samsung, who are also exploring new technologies for 7nm chips and beyond. While cautious about specific details, TSMC emphasizes its work with ASML on Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography for future nodes, acknowledging the challenges involved.

title: Is EUV Lithography Finally Ready?
summary: The semiconductor industry is buzzing about the potential readiness of Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography for chip production, following ASML Holding NV's announcement of orders from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. (TSMC) for advanced EUV systems. TSMC has achieved significant throughput milestones, exposing over 1,000 wafers in one day, indicating that EUV for 10-nanometer features might be closer to volume production than previously expected. Despite a history of delays and skepticism, ASML and its partners are addressing technical challenges, particularly with the light source, to make EUV a viable technology for next-generation logic, DRAM, and NAND flash memory production.

title: TSMC's chief financial officer Lora Ho says glass ceiling 'in your heart'
summary: Lora Ho, TSMC's chief financial officer, discusses her 30-year career in a male-dominated industry, managing US$46 billion in capital spending, and overseeing the company's tripling annual profit. She states that the "glass ceiling is in your heart" and attributes TSMC's financial success and market dominance to strong financial management. The article highlights TSMC's critical role in chip manufacturing for major tech companies like Apple and Qualcomm.

title: TSMC to have four EUV scanners in 2015, to use EUV tools for 10nm chips
summary: TSMC has ordered two additional EUV lithography scanners from ASML, bringing their total to four for 2015. These scanners will be used for the commercial production of 10nm chips using EUV lithography starting in 2016-2017. TSMC aims to leverage this advanced technology to gain an advantage over other foundries.

title: iPhone 6 and 6 Plus Use 20-Nanometer A8 Processor From TSMC
summary: Apple's new iPhone 6 and 6 Plus feature a 20-nanometer A8 processor manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), confirming earlier rumors. This shift reduces Apple's reliance on rival Samsung, which had previously manufactured chips like the A7. The 20-nanometer process offers higher speeds, a smaller chip, and less power consumption compared to the 28-nanometer predecessors.

title: TSIA tips growth for Taiwan semiconductor sector
summary: Taiwan's semiconductor industry is projected to achieve significant growth in 2014, with a 17.4 percent increase to NT$2.22 trillion (US$73.89 billion), outperforming the global average. This growth is driven by strong performances across its subsectors, particularly IC design and manufacturing, and is expected to benefit major firms like Advanced Semiconductor Engineering Inc., MediaTek Inc., and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. The global semiconductor market is also predicted to grow, fueled by demand from automobiles, smartphones, and tablets.

title: Growing InGaAs MOSCAPs directly on (100) silicon substrates
summary: Researchers in Taiwan have successfully produced indium gallium arsenide (InGaAs) metal-oxide-semiconductor capacitors (MOSCAPs) with low interface trap densities directly on (100) silicon substrates using metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD). This achievement, which involves growing the InGaAs heterostructure on 300mm silicon, represents a significant step towards integrating high-performance, low-power logic devices on common silicon platforms. The team from National Chiao-Tung University and TSMC demonstrated that their Al2O3/InGaAs/Si MOSCAPs achieved performance comparable to those on lattice-matched InP, highlighting their potential for future semiconductor manufacturing.

title: TSMC says Morris Chang is retiring as CEO — again
summary: TSMC announced that Morris Chang is retiring as CEO for the second time, appointing Mark Liu and Wei Che-chia as co-CEOs while Chang will remain chairman. The company also approved significant capital appropriations for technology upgrades and R&D. TSMC anticipates record capital spending this year and next.

title: Xilinx and TSMC Reach Volume Production on all 28nm CoWoS™-based All Programmable 3D IC Families
summary: Xilinx and TSMC announced that all Xilinx 28nm 3D IC families, including the Virtex-7 HT family, are now in volume production using TSMC's CoWoS™ process. This achievement solidifies Xilinx's leadership in 3D IC technology and positions them for future success with TSMC's 20SoC and 16FinFET processes. These advanced devices offer significant silicon scaling, power, and performance benefits for various high-performance applications.

title: Korea Economic Daily Archives
summary: This article discusses the ongoing rumor in 2013 regarding Apple's potential shift of chip production from Samsung to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). While various reports suggested a full transition, it was ultimately speculated that Samsung would retain a significant portion of A8 processor production due to TSMC's manufacturing difficulties.

title: Rumor: TSMC inks deal to build 20nm 'A8' chips for Apple starting this year
summary: A new report from DigiTimes suggests that Apple and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) have finalized a three-year agreement for TSMC to supply A-series chips for future iPhones and iPads. The deal reportedly includes plans for TSMC to build 20-nanometer, 16-nanometer, and 10-nanometer process nodes, with trial runs of 20nm "A8" chips expected to begin in July and substantial production ramping up by September for devices debuting in 2014. This move would allow Apple to reduce its reliance on rival Samsung as a chip supplier.

title: TSMC Takes on Samsung｜Industry｜2013-05-09
summary: TSMC, with soaring stock prices and record profits, has formed a "Grand Alliance" to compete against vertically integrated rivals Samsung and Intel. Chairman Morris Chang explains this strategy as a collaborative ecosystem involving customers, equipment manufacturers, and IP companies, emphasizing collective innovation and strength over mere size. This alliance, he argues, is better suited to navigate the increasing complexity of the semiconductor industry and capitalize on opportunities like the mobile device boom.

title: Apple bid for exclusive TSMC chip supply access denied, report says
summary: Apple reportedly offered Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) over $1 billion for exclusive chip production to diversify its supply chain away from Samsung, but TSMC denied the bid. TSMC wants to maintain flexibility and avoid dedicating facilities to a single client or product, despite strong sales from Apple's iPhone and iPad lines. TSMC stated their hesitation to tie up production facilities, though they currently supply Apple indirectly and through prior agreements for future chip production.

title: TSMC makes the future of 28nm a little brighter
summary: TSMC's 28nm process is now achieving an 80% yield, significantly improving the supply for 28nm GPUs and future APUs from companies like NVIDIA and AMD. Additionally, TSMC's new Fab 15 is set to massively expand production capacity, ensuring all major client demands for 28nm technology will be met by Q4 2012. This news signifies an end to previous supply shortages and a brighter outlook for the industry.

title: TSMC eyes future technology with $1.4bn ASML investment
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is investing 1.1bn euros ($1.4bn) in ASML, a key equipment supplier, to cut costs and develop tools for smaller, more cost-effective chips. This investment includes a 5% stake in ASML and aims to support the development of larger 450mm wafers and extreme ultraviolet lithography, technologies crucial for future chip manufacturing. Intel recently made a similar investment in ASML, highlighting the industry-wide push for these advancements.

title: Renesas Electronics and TSMC Collaborate to Construct Ecosystem for Microcontrollers
summary: Renesas Electronics and TSMC announced an extended collaboration on microcontroller (MCU) technology, moving to 40-nanometer (nm) embedded flash (eFlash) process technology for automotive and consumer applications. This partnership aims to combine Renesas' MONOS technology with TSMC's advanced CMOS processes to create an MCU ecosystem and ensure consistent supply and market expansion for MCU products. The collaboration also intends to make the MONOS process platform available to other semiconductor suppliers globally.

title: Renesas, Taiwan's TSMC Plan Chip Tie-up: Reports - Quick Facts
summary: Japanese chipmaker Renesas Electronics is reportedly planning a chip production tie-up with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) to reduce costs. TSMC is expected to produce chips for Renesas for use in automobiles and home appliances. Renesas has not yet provided specific details about the collaboration.

title: TSMC Solar receives UL, IEC and ISO 9001 certifications
summary: TSMC Solar Ltd., a subsidiary of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Inc., has received certifications from Underwriters Laboratories (UL) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) for its TS CIGS series photovoltaic modules, allowing its products to enter a majority of the world's solar markets. The company also secured ISO 9001 quality management system certification, with customer shipments scheduled to begin in April. These milestones were achieved within four months of completing tool move-in, demonstrating TSMC Solar's commitment to quality and manufacturing excellence.

title: TSMC finds its 28nm dance card a little overbooked
summary: TSMC is experiencing high demand for its 28nm chip manufacturing process, leading to concerns about its ability to meet orders from numerous customers including AMD, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, and Altera. This increased demand is partly due to AMD switching to TSMC from GLOBALFOUNDRIES for its next-generation chips after encountering yield problems. TSMC expects 28nm processes to contribute significantly to its revenues, growing from over 2% in late 2011 to over 10% in 2012.

title: AMD turns to TSMC for more Fusion chipsets
summary: AMD is reportedly contracting Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) for additional production of Fusion-based chipsets due to high demand. This move is expected to boost AMD's third-quarter revenue by 8 to 12 percent, building on previous quarters' success driven by Fusion APU shipments. Major retailers like Acer, Asus, Dell, and Quanta are already offering notebooks featuring AMD's APUs.

title: MOEA presentation: Taiwan's ICT industry development and outlook
summary: This presentation from Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) outlines the development and future outlook of Taiwan's key Information and Communication Technology (ICT) industries. It details the industry's historical growth, current market strengths in areas like PC, handset, display, and semiconductor sectors, and discusses future challenges and opportunities including global market shifts, competition, and emerging market focus. The presentation also highlights Taiwan's role in the global supply chain, its logistic power, and new business models like cloud computing and mobile device investments.

title: Giving Employees Their Lives Back｜Insight｜2011-02-24
summary: This article details how TSMC, under chairman Morris Chang, reduced its average employee workweek from 58 to 50 hours without sacrificing efficiency. Two key initiatives, reducing ineffectual meetings and leveraging technology to streamline work, were instrumental in this transformation. The change allowed employees to regain "quality hours" for their personal lives, setting a new standard for corporate culture in the tech industry.

title: Spreadtrum and TSMC Achieve 3G TD-SCDMA Baseband Processor Milestone
summary: Spreadtrum Communications and TSMC have successfully commercialized the world's first 40nm Time Division - Synchronous Code Division Multiple Access (TD-SCDMA) baseband processor. This achievement marks a significant milestone for 3G communication technology, especially for China's 3G standard, offering enhanced performance and power efficiency. The chip is now in initial production, demonstrating both companies' capabilities in advanced semiconductor design and manufacturing.

title: TSMC, NCKU and NUK Signed Cooperation Agreement to Promote Industry and Academia Corporation Program
summary: TSMC, National Cheng Kung University (NCKU), and National University of Kaohsiung (NUK) signed an agreement to foster semiconductor technology experts through an Industry and Academia Corporation Program (IACP). This initiative aims to integrate academic teaching resources with TSMC's industry expertise to cultivate national semiconductor talents and provide diverse learning opportunities for personnel. The program includes professional certification, advanced degrees, and practical experience for students and employees, enhancing semiconductor education and industry-university collaboration.

title: TSMC starts construction of Gigafab in Taiwan
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) has begun construction on its third 12-inch Gigafab, Fab 15, in Taiwan's Central Taiwan Science Park. This new facility will have a massive cleanroom area, a capacity exceeding 100,000 12-inch wafers per month, and will incorporate environmentally friendly concepts. The project represents an investment of over NT$300bn (US$9.4bn) and is expected to create 8,000 jobs.

title: First CMOS-compatible III-V n-MOSFET with self-aligned contacts
summary: Researchers from Singapore and Taiwan have developed the first CMOS-compatible III-V n-MOSFETs with self-aligned contacts, addressing a critical challenge for scaling integrated circuits beyond 22nm. This innovative process uses a GeSi layer and nickel reactions to create low-resistance ohmic contacts on GaAs, demonstrating a significant step towards mass-production of high-mobility III-V devices for next-generation electronics.

title: TSMC New Standard Cell Slim Library Reduces Logic Area 15%
summary: TSMC announced the introduction of its new Slim Library, which reduces system-on-chip (SoC) routed logic block area by 15% compared to current standard cell libraries. This library, developed under the AreaTrim collaboration with Tela Innovations, targets TSMC’s 65nm LP process technology and maintains equivalent performance and power while offering easy integration into existing design flows. It is available in limited release now and targets general release in Q1 2011.

title: TSMC Unveils Two New Reference Flows
summary: TSMC introduced Reference Flow 11.0 and Analog/Mixed Signal (AMS) Reference Flow 1.0, key components of its Open Innovation Platform™. Reference Flow 11.0 focuses on Electronic System Level (ESL) design, SoC Interconnect Fabric, and 2-D/3-D ICs using TSV technology, while AMS Reference Flow 1.0 addresses advanced multi-vendor AMS design and complexity at 40nm and 28nm nodes. These new flows enhance design capabilities, power efficiency, and time-to-market for complex semiconductor designs.

title: Qualcomm and TSMC Collaborating on 28nm Process Technology
summary: Qualcomm (Nasdaq: QCOM) and TSMC (TWSE: 2330, NYSE: TSM) announced their collaboration on 28 nanometer (nm) process technology to enable more functionality and lower power consumption in mobile devices. This advanced technology facilitates the integration of more features into smaller, cost-efficient chips, expanding wireless applications. The companies are leveraging their long-term relationship to migrate directly from 45nm to 28nm, with Qualcomm expecting to tape out its first commercial 28nm products in mid-2010.
